title: Conjugacy of the local Frobenius along the Frobenius orbit
statement:
Use the finite coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], so $X_0$ is separated finite type over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $(K,\varphi)$ be a strict Weil complex of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex], and let $x$ be a closed point of $X_0$ of degree $d=[\kappa(x):k_0]$. Write $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g=g_\gamma$ and $\sigma(c)=c^q$, $\gamma=\sigma^{-1}$ as in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. A lift of $x$ means a $k$-morphism $z:s\to X$ whose projection to $X_0$ has image $x$. Its stalk complex is $K_z=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*K)$, with [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].

The action on lifts induced by the semilinear scheme automorphism $g$ is
$$G(z)=g\circ z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma).$$
Thus the source is reparametrized so that $G(z)$ is again a $k$-morphism. For a geometric point $v:s\to X$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(k)$, write $r_{v,\alpha}:K_v\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{v\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)}$ for the canonical reparametrization: on represented stalk germs it sends $(U,u,a)$ to $(U,u\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha),a)$, using [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk].

1. There are exactly $d$ lifts of $x$. For any lift $z_0$, they are the distinct $z_i=G^i(z_0)$, $0\leq i<d$, and $z_{i+d}=z_i$. If $m\geq1$ and $d\mid m$, each $z_i$ is fixed by $\Phi^m$ and corresponds to a unique $y_i\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ above $x$ under [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points].
2. Put $\varphi^{[0]}=\mathrm{id}_K$ under the identity-pullback identification, extending [def-trf-iterated-weil-map]. For $i\geq0$, let $p_i=g^i\circ z_0$, and let $c_i:(Lg^{i*}K)_{z_0}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{p_i}$ be the canonical pullback-stalk comparison. Since $z_i=p_i\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^i)$, define
$$T_i^{z_0}=\varphi^{[i]}_{z_0}\circ c_i^{-1}\circ r_{p_i,\sigma^i}^{-1}:K_{z_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{z_0}.$$
These transports are canonical for the chosen starting lift and integer iterate (they are not asserted to be periodic in $i$). They satisfy $T_0^{z_0}=\mathrm{id}$ and
$$T_{i+j}^{z_0}=T_i^{z_0}\circ T_j^{z_i}\qquad(i,j\geq0),$$
the stalkwise cocycle of [lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle].
3. If $m\geq1$ and $d\mid m$, the local operators of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] satisfy
$$F_{y_i,m}=(T_i^{z_0})^{-1}\circ F_{y_0,m}\circ T_i^{z_0}.$$
Their categorical traces over $A$ agree. In particular the conjugacy class of the one-circuit operator $F_{y_0,d}$ is independent of the choice of $z_0$.

proof.text: The description of a geometric point in [def-weil-geometric-point], and the fibre-product universal property, identify lifts $z:s\to X$ over $k$ with $k_0$-embeddings $e:\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field], $L=\kappa(x)$ is finite over $k_0$. A basis of length $d$ identifies its underlying set with $k_0^d$, so $|L|=q^d$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius] to $L/k_0$: it is separable, and its automorphisms are the distinct $q$-power Frobenius powers $F^j$, $0\leq j<d$. There is an embedding $e_0:L\to k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed], since $k$ is algebraically closed and hence separably closed. Every embedding has image the unique $q^d$-element subfield of $k$, by [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure]. Thus $e\mapsto e_0^{-1}e$ identifies all embeddings with $\operatorname{Gal}(L/k_0)$; they are exactly $e_0F^j$, distinctly for $0\leq j<d$.

By [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], $g$ has affine map $a\otimes b\mapsto a\otimes\gamma(b)$. If $z$ corresponds to $e$, the affine map of $g\circ z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ is $a\otimes b\mapsto\sigma(e(a)\gamma(b))=e(a)^q b$. Thus $G$ sends $e$ to $eF$ and cycles precisely the $d$ embeddings found in step 1; in particular $G^d z=z$. For $d\mid m$, [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure] says every element of $e(L)=\mathbf F_{q^d}$ satisfies $t^{q^m}=t$ (iterate the $q^d$-power identity $m/d$ times). It also lies in $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, so $e$ factors uniquely through that fixed subfield and gives a rational point $y$. The affine formula for $\Phi$ gives $z^*\Phi^{m*}(a\otimes b)=e(a)^{q^m}b=e(a)b=z^*(a\otimes b)$. Hence $\Phi^m z=z$, and [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] identifies it with the indicated component. Conversely every rational point over $x$ gives such an embedding, so this accounts for all $y_i$.

source.place: Proof (1), with the semilinear action made explicit

proof.text: For any geometric point $v:s\to X$, reparametrizing each lift $u$ by $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal N_v\to\mathcal N_{v\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)}$ of the pointed-neighbourhood categories in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. Its inverse uses $\alpha^{-1}$ and it leaves every section and restriction map unchanged. Taking colimits gives $r_{v,\alpha}$, natural and $A$-linear. It gives $r_{v,1}=1$ and the composition law obtained by composing the two source reparametrizations; these hold on every represented germ. Apply this termwise to complexes: [lem-cbc-proetale-classical-stalk] makes the stalk functor exact, so these isomorphisms descend to the derived category. At $s$ and its identity point, $(s,\mathrm{id})$ is initial in the pointed-neighbourhood category (its unique map to $(U,u)$ is $u$), and hence terminal in the opposite category; the stalk colimit is therefore evaluation at $s$; by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] this is precisely $\operatorname{Fib}_s$.

source.place: Tag 0993, lemma-classical-point, and preceding exactness paragraph; reparametrization is the explicit isomorphism of the defining neighbourhood diagrams

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence] to finite constant $A=A_{E,n}$. It supplies the natural $A$-linear comparisons $c_{f,v,H}:(Lf^*H)_v\cong H_{fv}$ with their explicit germ normalization, composition and identity equations, and compatibility with the reparametrizations of step 3. In particular it gives $c_i=c_{g^i,z_0,K}$ from the statement. Its coherence equations apply to the powers of $g$ and the field automorphisms $\sigma^i$, including exponent zero. The coefficient identifications are the canonical ones preserving constant sections, as required by that lemma.

source.place: Tag 05V1, lemma-point-morphism-sites, and its explicit colimit proof (Tag 0F4F, lemma-point-functor); proetale.tex Tag 0993; composition is the cited pro-etale derived comparison

proof.text:
Apply step 4 with $f=g^i$, $v=z_0$, and step 3 to $z_i=g^iz_0\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^i)$. For any coefficient complex $H$ on $X$, abbreviate the resulting comparison by
$$Q_i^{v}(H)=c_{g^i,v,H}^{-1}\circ r_{g^iv,\sigma^i,H}^{-1}:H_{G^iv}\xrightarrow{\sim}(Lg^{i*}H)_v.$$
Steps 3–4 give, after the pullback-composition identification,
$$Q_{i+j}^{v}(H)=Q_i^{v}(Lg^{j*}H)\circ Q_j^{G^iv}(H).$$
Indeed both sides take a germ at $G^{i+j}v=g^{i+j}v\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^{i+j})$, remove the source reparametrization by $\sigma^{i+j}$, and insert the same section in the iterated base-change neighbourhood of $v$; removing $\sigma^j$ followed by $\sigma^i$ gives $\sigma^{i+j}$ and the projections agree by step 4. Naturality gives
$$Q_i^{v}(K)\circ\varphi^{[j]}_{G^iv}=(Lg^{i*}\varphi^{[j]})_v\circ Q_i^{v}(Lg^{j*}K).$$
By [def-trf-iterated-weil-map], $T_i^v=\varphi^{[i]}_vQ_i^v(K)$ is invertible. For $i,j\geq1$, the preceding two equalities and [lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle] give the explicitly typed calculation
$$\begin{aligned}
T_i^vT_j^{G^iv}
&=\varphi^{[i]}_vQ_i^v(K)\varphi^{[j]}_{G^iv}Q_j^{G^iv}(K)\\
&=\varphi^{[i]}_v(Lg^{i*}\varphi^{[j]})_vQ_i^v(Lg^{j*}K)Q_j^{G^iv}(K)\\
&=\varphi^{[i+j]}_vQ_{i+j}^v(K)=T_{i+j}^v.
\end{aligned}$$
Each side maps $K_{G^{i+j}v}$ to $K_v$. For a zero index, $\varphi^{[0]}=1$ and the identity comparisons in steps 3–4 give $Q_0=1$, so $T_0=1$ and the same equation follows. No periodicity of $T_i$ is used.

source.place: Proof (2), with the missing zero-iterate convention and reparametrizations supplied

proof.text:
Let $d\mid m$ and $z=z_i$. Step 2 gives $G^mz=z$, so $w=g^mz=z\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^m)$ and $w\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^m)=z$. By [def-trf-frobenius-operators], $\tau_{y,m}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*\kappa^{(m)}_K)\circ\rho_{y,m}$, where $\rho$ uses $\Phi^mz=z$. By [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization], $\Phi^m=g^mF_X^{am}$. The specified comparison of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] is the absolute-Frobenius trivialization of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] applied to $H=L(g^m)^*K$. Apply [lem-trf-frobenius-stalk-trivialization-normalization] with $b=am$: on $s$, $\delta=F_s^{am}=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^m)$, and its germ formula removes $\delta$ from the source while retaining the section. Through the composition and reparametrization equations of [lem-trf-proetale-pullback-stalk-coherence] (step 4) this is $r_{w,\sigma^m}^{-1}:K_{w\delta}=K_z\to K_w$. Thus
$$c_{g^m,z,K}\circ\tau_{y,m}=r_{w,\sigma^m}^{-1},\qquad F_{y,m}=\varphi^{[m]}_z\circ c_{g^m,z,K}^{-1}\circ r_{w,\sigma^m}^{-1}=T_m^z.$$
Here $A$ is finite and killed by a power of $\ell\ne p$, invertible in $k$, so the comparison hypotheses hold. No equality $g^mz=z$ of raw scheme morphisms is used.

source.place: Specified absolute-Frobenius trivialization in the proof; pullback naturality and relative-Frobenius normalization in lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback; Stacks Tag 0F6W (lemma-relative-frobenius-weakly-etale)

proof.text:
Use step 5 twice and step 6 at $z_0$ and $z_i$. As morphisms $K_{z_i}\to K_{z_0}$, the two factorizations are
$$T_i^{z_0}\circ F_{y_i,m}=T_i^{z_0}\circ T_m^{z_i}=T_{i+m}^{z_0}=T_{m+i}^{z_0}=T_m^{z_0}\circ T_i^{z_m}=F_{y_0,m}\circ T_i^{z_0},$$
where $z_m=z_0$ is an equality of normalized $k$-points. Left-compose with $(T_i^{z_0})^{-1}$ to obtain exactly $F_{y_i,m}=(T_i^{z_0})^{-1}F_{y_0,m}T_i^{z_0}$. In particular every arrow in the calculation has the required source and target.

source.place: Proof (3), replacing the ill-typed conjugate by the displayed intertwining calculation

proof.text: Apply the geometric-stalk clause of [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness] with $\bar x=z_i:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ and $\Omega=k$. The underlying complex of a strict Weil complex is in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, and the structure morphism of $X$ is separated finite type by the coefficient conventions, with $A=A_{E,n}$ and $n\geq1$. That clause asserts perfectness of the ordinary-module complex $R\Gamma(s_{\mathrm{proet}},Lz_i^*K)$, with $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ explicitly meaning bounded finite-projective complexes. By the exact-sections identification in step 3, this is precisely $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz_i^*K)=K_{z_i}$ used here. Thus each $K_{z_i}$ is perfect; bounded finite cohomology alone is not the input to the trace law. Apply conjugacy invariance from [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws] with $P_1=K_{z_i}$, $P_2=K_{z_0}$, $w=T_i^{z_0}$, $v_1=F_{y_i,m}$ and $v_2=F_{y_0,m}$; step 7 gives its intertwining hypothesis. The traces are equal. With $m=d$, every possible initial lift is a $z_i$ by step 1, so the same equation proves independence of the one-circuit conjugacy class.

source.place: Proof (3), trace and one-circuit independence conclusions
